keyVerseText: And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS.
rootMeaning: The Greek word τίτλος (títlos) is of Latin origin, derived from titulus, meaning a title or inscription. This origin highlights its primary function as a label or identifying mark, often physically inscribed or displayed. Unlike the broader English term 'title,' which can be abstract or honorary, τίτλος emphasizes a concrete inscription or placard that conveys a specific identification or declaration.
usageInScripture: The word τίτλος appears only twice in the New Testament, consistently translated as 'title' or 'a title.' Its limited but focused usage underscores its role as a literal inscription rather than a metaphorical or honorary designation. This consistency in translation reveals the term's primary function as a physical label or identifying sign, particularly in contexts where written identification is crucial.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding τίτλος as a literal inscription enriches our grasp of how truth and identity are communicated in Scripture. The physicality of a title or placard points to the reality that Jesus' identity and mission were publicly declared and displayed, even in His suffering. This underscores the Christian conviction that Christ's kingship and messianic role are not hidden but openly proclaimed. The use of τίτλος reminds believers that the gospel message is meant to be seen and acknowledged, affirming Jesus as the King of the Jews and Savior of all.
keyVerseReflection: In John 19:19, 'And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS,' the word τίτλος signifies the formal inscription placed above Jesus during His crucifixion. This title was not merely a label but a declaration of His identity and the charge against Him. The use of τίτλος here emphasizes the public and undeniable nature of Jesus' kingship, even as He was crucified, fulfilling the prophetic and redemptive purposes of His mission.
